title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Nonimmigrant Work Visa Classifications
source: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Department of Homeland Security
content:
Foreign nationals seeking temporary employment in the United States must qualify under specific nonimmigrant visa classifications sponsored by a U.S. employer filing Form I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker).

Key categories include H-1B (Specialty Occupations requiring a higher education degree or equivalent), L-1 (Intracompany Transferees in executive, managerial, or specialized knowledge roles), and O-1 (Individuals with Extraordinary Ability or Achievement in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics).

Upon approval by USCIS, prospective workers apply for visa stamping at a U.S. Embassy or Consulate abroad before admission at a U.S. port of entry. At arrival, Customs and Border Protection (CBP) issues an electronic Form I-94 documenting lawful status and expiration date.

title: Social Security Administration (SSA) Social Security Numbers for Noncitizens
content:
A Social Security Number (SSN) is a nine-digit number issued to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and temporary foreign workers authorized to work in the United States.

An SSN is required to work lawfully, receive wages, pay federal and state taxes, and build a domestic credit profile. Noncitizens authorized to work under statuses such as H-1B, L-1, or post-completion OPT can apply at a local Social Security card center.

Required documentation includes an unexpired foreign passport, U.S. visa, Form I-94 arrival record, and employment verification letter. The SSA verifies lawful presence directly with USCIS SAVE system before issuing the card, which is delivered by mail within 2 to 4 weeks.

title: Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) New York City Subway and OMNY Contactless Fare System
publisher: State of New York / City of New York
content:
The Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) operates the New York City transit network, including the 24-hour New York City Subway, MTA Bus network, Staten Island Railway, Long Island Rail Road (LIRR), and Metro-North Railroad.

Subway and local bus travel costs a flat fare of $2.90 per ride. Riders pay using OMNY (One Metro New York) by tapping contactless debit/credit cards, smart devices (Apple Pay, Google Wallet), or dedicated OMNY cards at turnstiles.

OMNY features automatic weekly fare capping: once a rider pays for 12 rides using the same card or device between Monday and Sunday, all remaining subway and local bus rides for the rest of that seven-day period are free. Free transfers between subway and local buses occur automatically within two hours of tapping.

title: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) Tenant Rights and Leases
source: NYC Department of Housing Preservation & Development (HPD) / NYS Homes and Community Renewal
content:
Residential leases in New York City are subject to the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (HSTPA). Under New York State law, security deposits are strictly capped at no more than one month's rent.

Landlords are legally prohibited from requiring advance rent exceeding one month or charging application fees above $20 for background and credit checks. Approximately one million apartments in NYC are rent-stabilized, meaning annual rent increases are legally limited by the NYC Rent Guidelines Board.

Tenants have the right to habitable living conditions, including heat and hot water regulations (the 'Heat Season' from October 1 to May 31), smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and protection against unlawful lockouts or harassment.
